topic.angle: vol-targeting, inverse-vol weighting, downside deviation scaling

papers.title: Enhanced Momentum Strategies
papers.hypothesis: Replace standard momentum signal with semi-volatility-scaled momentum (stock formation return divided by its realized downside standard deviation over the formation window), which reduces crash exposure and raises Sharpe versus equal-vol scaling.
papers.rationale: Hanauer & Windmüller (2022, JBF) test cMOM, sMOM, and dMOM across 48 country universes and find semi-vol scaling (sMOM) narrowly outperforms standard vol scaling by preserving upside vol in the denominator. For a cross-sectional ranker, replacing the raw 12-1 return rank with (return / semi-vol) is a one-line change with empirically documented Sharpe improvement of ~0.15–0.25 in U.S. data. Negative skewness and crash frequency both drop materially.

papers.title: Momentum is Still There Conditional on Volatility-Amplified Pessimism
papers.hypothesis: Attenuate or zero out cross-sectional momentum exposure when realized market volatility (e.g., 21-day rolling) and an investor pessimism proxy (e.g., put-call ratio or VIX term structure slope) are simultaneously elevated, restoring alpha in calm or optimistic regimes.
papers.rationale: Ghazi, Schneider & Strauss (2023, SSRN 4680094) show that the joint interaction of high market vol and high pessimism is the key predictor of momentum failure — neither alone is sufficient. This maps directly to a binary or smooth scaling factor applied to position weights: full exposure in low-vol or optimistic regimes, reduced/zero in the joint-high regime. The fear-and-greed data already loaded in this repo (data/*.parquet) could proxy pessimism cheaply.

papers.title: All Days Are Not Created Equal: Understanding Momentum by Learning to Weight Past Returns
papers.hypothesis: Compute the formation-period momentum signal as a weighted sum of daily returns, assigning higher weights to days that coincide with earnings announcements or large cross-sectional market jumps, and lower weights to calm mid-period days.
papers.rationale: Beckmeyer & Wiedemann (2025, JBF) use a machine-learning approach to recover which days in the 12-month window most predict future returns; earnings announcement days and market-wide jump days receive the highest weights. The practical implementation is a simple day-type lookup: tag each past trading day as 'event' (earnings ±1, |market return| > 1.5%) vs 'normal', then weight returns 3–5× higher on event days when computing the stock-level signal. The paper shows this subsumes standard 12-1 momentum and is robust through the most recent decade.

papers.title: Volatility Targeting Is Trendy: How Trend Following Explains Alpha in Volatility-Managed Strategies
papers.hypothesis: Scale each selected stock's position weight by inverse realized 21-day volatility (individual stock level, not portfolio level), so that high-vol winners receive smaller allocations and low-vol winners receive larger ones, capturing the implicit trend/momentum benefit of vol targeting documented for equity.
papers.rationale: Hood & Raughtigan (2024, SSRN 4773781) decompose vol-targeting alpha and show that for equities the entire excess comes from an embedded trend/momentum tilt created by the leverage effect (high-vol periods follow down-moves). Applied at stock level within an already-ranked cross-sectional portfolio, this modifies allocation weights — not ranking — which is an additive change that avoids disturbing the signal construction. The 21-day lookback for vol estimation is a well-documented sweet spot balancing responsiveness and noise.

papers.title: Momentum, Market Volatility, and Reversal
papers.hypothesis: Standard cross-sectional momentum underperforms and reverts to contrarian in high-realized-market-volatility regimes; a regime-switching strategy that flips to reversal when trailing 60-day market vol exceeds the 70th percentile improves returns, but the switching adds turnover and timing risk.
papers.rationale: Butt, Kolari & Sadaqat (2023, SSRN 4342008) confirm that momentum profits collapse and reverse specifically when preceding 60-day market volatility is elevated above historical norms. This is a negative result for pure always-on momentum, but the regime-conditioning insight is actionable: a simpler implementation is to reduce portfolio size (top_n_pct) or hold_days in high-vol regimes rather than flip to reversal, which avoids adding a contrarian overlay that may behave differently in a long-only constrained universe.
